note: Corroboration for 'plain function, no args' from outside the house harness. See the post's 'What went wrong with these numbers' section.

wall_vs_cpu_time.means: If these agree, the timed windows are not losing time to preemption, so a slow result means slow cycles rather than an interrupted measurement.

machine_speed.kernel: zero-argument Python function call, measured by bench() at its default sub-microsecond plan

august_harness_note: The harness as it stood for the published run is recoverable with `git show 27abde4:experiments/lib/bench.py`. Run against this experiment on 2026-09-03 it reported 48.9 ns for a plain call, against 36.2 ns from the current harness and 37.2 ns from timeit the same afternoon -- all three far from the 13.4 ns published on 2026-08-29.
